To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the response functions of neutron matter are well described within an effective field theory based on a momentum expansion, that the density fluctuations of the Fermi-liquid lead to exciton bound states, that the spin fluctuations are diffusive above the pair-breaking energy threshold, and that the specific heat of the neutron matter is dominated by the collective pair-breaking mode at temperatures of the order of 0.5 MeV and densities of 10^11 g/cm^3.

the response of a Fermi-liquid system of interacting fermions to density and spin perturbations is characterized by the existence of undamped collective modes in the density channel and by diffusive modes in the spin channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the response properties of cold neutron matter to density and spin perturbations, and the associated collective excitations.
the properties of a single-component Fermi-liquid at low temperatures and low densities.
the properties of a strongly interacting Fermi system at low temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the response of cold neutron matter to perturbative density and spin fluctuations is dominated by the collective excitations of pair-correlated Fermi-liquids.
the response properties of cold neutron matter are qualitatively similar to those of the degenerate electronic gas.

the neutron matter response is characterized by a very rich spectrum of collective excitations, with the density fluctuations leading to undamped excitons and the spin excitations leading to diffusive modes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the response functions of neutron matter at low temperatures are dominated by the pair-breaking modes, which are associated with the breaking of Cooper pairs and the formation of quasiparticles.
the response of cold Fermi liquids to density perturbations is qualitatively different from that to spin perturbations.
the response of cold neutron matter is determined by the competition between the kinetic energy and the pairing energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to the conventional wisdom, a single-component Fermi liquid at low temperatures is not a good approximation for neutron matter at densities relevant to the physics of neutron stars.
the collective excitations in cold neutron matter are not Landau quasiparticles, and their spectral properties are very different from those of the quasiparticles in the degenerate electron system.
a pair-correlated Fermi liquid can be a good model of cold neutron matter at sub-nuclear densities.
